approachQuestion.prompt:
Merge ordered feeds

Two arrays are each already sorted nondecreasing. Return one sorted array containing all elements, preserving duplicates. 0≤m,n≤200000; values are signed 32-bit. Examples: [1,4,4]+[2,4]→[1,2,4,4,4]; []+[3]→[3].

Do not modify either input. Values are opaque comparison keys; hashing, radix, counting and bucket methods are outside the stated model. Choose the most efficient valid method that returns the required result for every allowed input.
constraints: Inputs are read-only and must remain unchanged.
Only comparison-based ordering is allowed; hashing, radix, counting and bucket methods are outside this problem model.

options.text: Advance one pointer in each input, append the smaller current value, then append the remaining suffix.
options.feedback: Each array’s existing order allows a linear merge without reordering either input.

options.text: Concatenate both arrays and sort the result.
options.feedback: Correct, but it discards useful existing order and performs unnecessary comparisons.

options.text: Append all values from the first input, then all from the second.
options.feedback: The result need not be sorted: [1,4]+[2,3].

options.text: For every output position, scan both arrays from their beginnings for the smallest unused value.
options.feedback: Correct but repeatedly revisits elements already known to be ordered.

feedback.reason: The smaller current head is the next output value because neither sorted suffix contains an earlier one.
details: Merge the two sorted inputs with two advancing indices, then copy the unconsumed suffix.

The smaller current head is the next output value because neither sorted suffix contains an earlier one. Exhausting one feed leaves the other's entire tail to copy; output size depends on both lengths.
“Advance one pointer in each input, append the smaller current value, then append the remaining suffix.”: Each array’s existing order allows a linear merge without reordering either input.
“Concatenate both arrays and sort the result.”: Correct, but it discards useful existing order and performs unnecessary comparisons.
“Append all values from the first input, then all from the second.”: The result need not be sorted: [1,4]+[2,3].
“For every output position, scan both arrays from their beginnings for the smallest unused value.”: Correct but repeatedly revisits elements already known to be ordered.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze the revealed two-input merge. Let m and n be the two input lengths. The result array is preallocated and excluded from auxiliary space, as are the input arrays. Count only the two indices and scalar temporary values; there is no recursion, copying of input arrays, or hashing. Comparisons and array writes are constant-time. Choose the tightest worst-case bounds.

options.text: O((m+n) log(m+n)) time, O(m+n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Consume every entry once without allocating a helper merge buffer.
details: Every head selection consumes one input element, and the suffix step copies all remaining entries. Exactly m+n returned values are written, giving O(m+n) time. Only two input indices and an output index are helper state. Sorting already ordered feeds adds unnecessary work; counting returned storage gives the wrong auxiliary-space dimension.
